attempts.summary: On node1, created user datauser and a dedicated loop-mounted XFS filesystem (/srv/img/data-quota.img) mounted at /srv/data with the usrquota option, then set an XFS user quota (bsoft=bhard=100m) for datauser via xfs_quota. Persisted the mount in /etc/fstab. Verified filesystem-level enforcement both before and after a full node restart: writes up to 100MB succeed, writes beyond 100MB are rejected by the kernel with "Disk quota exceeded". Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id (809708f3-1c5f-4e37-ad6a-8bcbae408799), issued a non-blocking shutdown -r now, polled until node1 was reachable again, confirmed a new boot_id (89834fbd-ce98-4d4d-804f-60fa9caa8bb1) and new uptime -s (2026-09-29 vs prior 2026-08-26), and re-verified the quota mount, quota limits, and live enforcement recovered automatically via fstab.
